title: Variant hot-swap: zero-downtime model variant hot-swap design spec
author: Aisha Chen
content:
Overview
======
This design spec describes the Variant Hot-Swap system: a runtime capability that allows swapping a serving model variant with zero client-visible downtime and bounded impact to SLOs. Hot-swap covers both in-place binary/weights replacement on a host and coordinated cross-host handoff for multi-replica services. The goal is to support fast rollbacks, emergency variant patches, and model upgrades without dropping connections or causing request errors.

Context and motivation
----------------------
- Customers require predictable service levels during model rollouts. Traditional rolling restarts or drain-and-replace strategies cause request queueing, increased latency, or transient errors.
- We already support progressive rollouts (canaries, staged traffic shifting). Hot-swap is a complementary capability targeted at: emergency rollbacks, tiny-critical fixes to a model in prod, and metadata-driven in-server variant swaps for affinity-sensitive sessions.

Goals
-----
1. Zero client-connection interruption for active sessions during a variant swap.
2. Maintain per-tenant latency 95th percentile within a configurable delta (default +200ms) during swaps.
3. Guarantee token-consistency for streaming sessions: no duplicated or missing tokens delivered to the client.
4. Support seamless rollback to the previous variant within 30s under normal conditions.
5. Provide observability hooks and automated runbook triggers on SLO deviations.

Non-goals
---------
- Solving stateful model weight warmup for very large models (>1TB) in sub-minute timelines. For very large variants, hot-swap will default to a staged cross-host approach rather than in-memory replace.
- Replacing major architecture changes that require incompatible runtime kernels; those will use progressive rolling upgrade paths.

Stakeholders and ownership
--------------------------
- Product: Model delivery and runtime experience (primary contact: Elena Moreno).
- Engineering: Serving runtime (owner), rollout orchestration, and SRE (SLO/alerting).
- Applied ML: Variant packaging constraints and validation tests.
- Customer Success: Communication templates for emergency changes.

High-level design
-----------------
The hot-swap capability is a multi-layer system composed of:
- HotSwap Controller (stateless service): accepts swap requests, validates policy, coordinates with orchestrator.
- Local Swap Agent (per-host): performs in-memory swap when safe, handles KV-cache migration, and sequences drain flags for local threads.
- Session Coordinator (distributed): ensures streaming sessions' token state is checkpointed and resumed without duplication across variant boundaries.
- Fallback Manager: enforces automatic rollback policies if SLO/health signals cross thresholds.

Sequence flows (in-place hot-swap)
---------------------------------
1. Operator or automated job creates a HotSwap request with target variant id, prewarm hints, and rollout policy.
2. HotSwap Controller verifies compatibility matrix and quota checks.
3. Controller instructs candidate hosts' Local Swap Agent to prewarm weights into an isolated address space (worker pool).
4. Local Swap Agent loads weights into standby workers, runs validation prompt set (configurable), and warms KV caches for prefix patterns if provided.
5. When 90% of standby workers pass validation, Controller issues a coordinated handoff: 
   a. Mark new workers as READY and old workers as TRANSITIONING.
   b. Session Coordinator freezes streaming token emission checkpoint per-session.
   c. Router starts routing new requests to READY workers.
   d. For active streaming sessions, last-token markers are emitted, session state copied to new worker, and emission resumes.
6. Local Swap Agent retires old workers post-grace period and releases memory.

Cross-host staged hot-swap (for large variants)
-----------------------------------------------
- If in-place memory constraints prevent instant replacement, the Controller performs a staggered handoff: bring up READY workers on different hosts, start routing a subset of new sessions, migrate long-lived sessions in small batches, and finally decommission old capacity.

Configuration table: key knobs
----------------------------
| config_name | default | description |
|-------------|---------|-------------|
| swap.max_downtime_ms | 200 | Soft upper bound for allowed p95 delta during swap |
| swap.prewarm_timeout_s | 60 | Time to wait for prewarm/validation before abort |
| swap.stream_checkpoint_mode | full | \"full\" or \"light\" checkpointing for streaming sessions |
| swap.rollback_on_slo | true | Whether to trigger automatic rollback on SLO breach |
| swap.max_parallel_sessions_migrate | 50 | Max concurrent session migrations per host |

Example HotSwap request (YAML)
------------------------------
```yaml
variant_id: v3.2.1-patch
prewarm_hints:
  - prompt_set: safety-smoke-10
  - warm_prefixes: ["/chat/", "/assist/"]
rollout_policy:
  strategy: in_place
  max_concurrent_migrations: 40
  p95_latency_delta_ms: 200
  abort_on_error: true
```

Failure modes and mitigations
-----------------------------
- Prewarm failure (OOM or validation fail): abort swap, mark variant as failed; send automatic rollback and create incident if >3 hosts failed.
- Partial migration stalls: backoff and reduce batch size; route new sessions away from affected hosts.
- Token duplication on streams: Session Coordinator enforces idempotent markers; API layer verifies last_token_id before resuming.
- Sudden SLO regressions: Fallback Manager initiates rollback and throttles new requests for affected tenant(s).

Observability and telemetry
-------------------------
Mandatory metrics (exported by Local Swap Agent and Controller):
- hot_swap.start_count, hot_swap.success_count, hot_swap.abort_count
- hot_swap.prewarm_latency_seconds (histogram)
- host.swap_memory_peak_bytes
- session.migrated_count, session.migration_latency_seconds
- per-tenant.p95_latency_delta_during_swap_ms (derived)
Alerts and runbook triggers:
- hot_swap.abort_rate > 5% in 10m -> Pager to serving-runtime-oncall
- per-tenant.p95_latency_delta_during_swap_ms > config.swap.max_downtime_ms -> Auto-rollback and SRE runbook

API contract and admin UX
------------------------
HotSwap API endpoints (REST):
- POST /hot-swap -> submit request; returns job id
- GET /hot-swap/{id}/status -> progress, per-host status
- POST /hot-swap/{id}/abort -> abort and rollback
Admin UX elements: validation results, per-host prewarm logs, and a safe-preview mode that runs validation without committing swap.

Runtime compatibility matrix (summary)
-------------------------------------
- In-place hot-swap supported: small->medium variants (<120GB resident) on kernels v2.1+.
- Cross-host staged hot-swap required for >120GB or incompatible kernel combos.
- Quantized variants: hot-swap allowed if kernel supports identical inference path; otherwise staged path.

Testing strategy and acceptance criteria
--------------------------------------
1. Unit tests for Local Swap Agent state transitions.
2. Integration: synthetic traffic runner with streaming sessions verifies no token duplication and p95 within configured delta across 1000 simulated long-lived sessions.
3. Chaos tests: randomly kill workers during handoff; system must rollback cleanly and record artifacts.
4. Performance: cold prewarm + swap on standard host must complete within prewarm_timeout_s for 95% of runs.
Acceptance: in 10 controlled rollouts, 0 client-visible disconnects and p95 within configured delta for 9/10 runs.

Rollout plan
-----------
- Phase 1 (canary): internal tenants only; runbook and monitoring enabled; 2-week window.
- Phase 2 (beta): selected customers opt-in for emergency hot-swap; gather telemetry and refine config knobs.
- Phase 3 (GA): enabled for all dedicated and hosted clusters with safe defaults and opt-out for tenants that request scheduled rolling upgrades.

Operational runbook (high-level)
-------------------------------
1. Check job status in Controller UI.
2. If prewarm failing: examine host logs, memory, and validation harness results.
3. On SLO breach: trigger abort -> Controller posts abort -> Fallback Manager starts rollback.
4. Postmortem: collect hot_swap.* metrics, agent logs, session checkpoint traces, and create incident summary.

Open design issues and follow-ups
--------------------------------
- Edge-case: long-running streaming sessions with external side effects (webhooks). Need a policy for tie-breaker: prefer session affinity vs. external-side-effect consistency.
- Validation set coverage: how to identify a minimal smoke set that covers critical safety/fidelity regressions for hot-swap. Responsible: Applied ML to own and curate.

References
----------
- Progressive variant rollouts (compat matrix) — see related page.
- Canary scheduler economics and rollback spec — see related page.

Appendix: small glossary
-----------------------
- READY worker: process/worker that has loaded a new variant and passed validation but not yet serving live traffic.
- TRANSITIONING worker: worker in the process of handing off state and draining outstanding requests.
- Session Coordinator: distributed component that manages streaming token checkpoints to coordinate migration.
